0. Getting started

David Sarrat González

Source: vignettes/book-00-start.Rmd
book-00-start.Rmd

What you will learn

Install the packages, load the practice data and open a connection.

Before you start

You need R 4.1 or newer and internet access for installation and the data download. RStudio is a convenient editor; ordinary R also works. The lessons use synthetic data and a local DataSHIELD server provided by DSLite. The results teach analysis methods; they are not clinical findings.

Run this installation block once. It installs the client, the local server and the packages used throughout the book. Installation is not executed here.

install.packages(c("remotes", "DSI", "DSOpal", "DSLite", "DBI", "RSQLite",
                   "resourcer", "withr", "openssl", "jsonlite", "knitr",
                   "rmarkdown", "duckdb", "lme4"))
remotes::install_github("datashield/dsBase@6.3.5", upgrade = "never")
remotes::install_github("datashield/dsBaseClient@6.3.5", upgrade = "never")
remotes::install_github("isglobal-brge/dsOMOP@2.10.5", upgrade = "never")
remotes::install_github("isglobal-brge/dsOMOPClient@2.10.5", upgrade = "never")

The client runs on your computer. The server runs requests near the data; DSLite lets you run both locally for practice.

Get the book helpers

Download book-helpers.zip, leave it zipped, and select it when the file chooser opens. This creates your working folder:

book_dir <- path.expand("~/book-work")
dir.create(book_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
unzip(file.choose(), exdir = book_dir)
setwd(book_dir)

The ZIP creates tools/book/ inside book-work. In each new R session, run setwd(path.expand("~/book-work")) before starting a chapter.

The helpers open the practice connection and print summaries as readable tables. connection.R supplies book_connect(), book_switch() and book_disconnect(); display.R supplies the display functions. Each chapter shows which files to source. No patient rows are fetched by the display helpers.

Check the client 

library(dsOMOPClient)
vapply(c("dsOMOPClient", "dsOMOP", "DSI", "DSLite", "dsBaseClient"),
       function(package) as.character(packageVersion(package)), character(1))
#> dsOMOPClient       dsOMOP          DSI       DSLite dsBaseClient 
#>     "2.10.5"     "2.10.5"      "1.8.0"      "1.5.0"      "6.3.5"

These are the packages installed on your computer. This check catches a missing package before you connect; it does not establish that a remote server is ready.

Load two public synthetic datasets

GiBleed supplies the people, visits, conditions and medicines for the first chapters. Synthea27Nj supplies numeric lab values and units. GiBleed has no numeric lab values, so the lab chapters use Synthea27Nj.

Run the loader once from book-work. It downloads the public Eunomia datasets and prepares the two local databases. We keep only its short data summary on screen:

source("tools/book/load-practice.R")
loader_log <- capture.output(data_info <- load_book_practice("../practice-data"))
knitr::kable(do.call(rbind, lapply(data_info, function(x)
  data.frame(Dataset = x$dataset, People = x$tables$person,
    Measurements = x$measurements$rows,
    `Numeric values` = x$measurements$numeric_values, check.names = FALSE))),
  row.names = FALSE)
Dataset People Measurements Numeric values
GiBleed 2694 44053 0
Synthea27Nj 28 10040 9107

GiBleed has 2,694 people and 44,053 measurement rows, but zero numeric values. Synthea27Nj has 28 people and 10,040 measurement rows, including 9,107 numeric values. These are exact counts because you are loading public synthetic data, acting as its custodian. An analyst’s protected query later reports 44,050 for GiBleed’s measurement rows: the lower end of a five-row band. The source data use the Apache-2.0 licence; keep that licence with redistributed copies.

The questionnaire dataset

The categorical, date and mortality lessons use a separate synthetic dataset: 48 people in four groups of twelve. Two groups answer the education question twice, swapping Secondary and University between their first and last answers. One group has only a birth year; one has neither visits nor a death record. The following table describes the public teaching data before any analysis:

source("tools/book/fixture.R")
knitr::kable(book_fixture_structure())
Item Total Female Male
People 48 20 28
Education respondents 24 10 14
Education answer rows 48 20 28
Fever answer rows 24 10 14
Inpatient visits 24 10 14
Outpatient visits 36 14 22
2023: myocardial infarction 12 4 8
2023: pneumonia 6 3 3
2024: myocardial infarction 12 4 8
2024: pneumonia 6 3 3
Survivors 12 6 6

There are 24 education respondents but 48 education answer rows: an answer row is not a person. There are 18 deaths in each of 2023 and 2024, and 12 survivors. The sex columns add to each total and let you predict later count tables. Some later exercises add medicine histories or duplicate weights; those sections explain the added data when needed.

Open the practice server

Each chapter starts with its own setup block. Copy it as shown:

source("tools/book/display.R")
source("tools/book/connection.R")
practice <- book_connect("gibleed")
conns <- practice$conns

conns holds the connection, not patient rows. The resource name gibleed selects the database; numeric and questionnaire select the other datasets.

ds.omop.server.version(conns = conns)[c("server", "published", "running", "ready")]
#>   server published running ready
#> 1   site    2.10.5  2.10.5  TRUE

ready confirms that the server’s running package and available methods agree. This checks the server installation, independently of the selected database.

Connect to your Opal server

Your administrator supplies the server URL, your user and password (or token), the project-qualified resource names and the DataSHIELD profile. The server is already set up. For a single-site lesson, replace the chapter’s local connection lines with this block, keeping its display.R source line:

library(dsOMOPClient)
library(DSOpal)
builder <- DSI::newDSLoginBuilder()
builder$append(server = "site", url = "<server-url>",
  user = "<user>", password = "<password>",
  driver = "OpalDriver", profile = "<profile>")
conns <- DSI::datashield.login(builder$build(), assign = FALSE)
ds.omop.connect(resource = "<project>.<gibleed-resource>", conns = conns)

Keep credentials outside shared scripts. If you receive a token, replace the user and password arguments with token = "<token>". The analysis calls use the same conns; your study data will give different results.

Where a practice chapter uses book_switch(), use the corresponding resource name supplied by your administrator instead:

ds.omop.disconnect(conns = conns)
ds.omop.connect(resource = "<project>.<numeric-resource>", conns = conns)

This attaches another database through the existing login.

Connect to two Opal sites

For the paired analyses in chapters 14, 16, 20 and 23, use two resources supplied by their administrators. Replace only practice_pair <- book_connect(...) and two_conns <- practice_pair$conns with this block. Keep the chapter’s package and helper source lines. In chapters 14 and 16, also keep the earlier single-site conns connection: later exercises still use its tables.

library(dsOMOPClient)
library(DSOpal)
builder <- DSI::newDSLoginBuilder()
builder$append(server = "north", url = "<server-a-url>",
  user = "<user-a>", password = "<password-a>",
  driver = "OpalDriver", profile = "<profile-a>")
builder$append(server = "south", url = "<server-b-url>",
  user = "<user-b>", password = "<password-b>",
  driver = "OpalDriver", profile = "<profile-b>")
two_conns <- DSI::datashield.login(builder$build(), assign = FALSE)
ds.omop.connect(
  resource = list(north = "<project-a>.<resource-a>",
                  south = "<project-b>.<resource-b>"),
  conns = two_conns, symbol = "book_pool")

north and south are the connection labels used by these lessons, not required geographical locations. Each resource-list name matches a login-builder name. book_pool is the server-side name of the attached OMOP handle; subsequent calls use that name together with two_conns. Chapters 14, 16 and 23 need lab resources; chapter 20 needs drug and outcome data. Use distinct study populations when pooling.

Chapters 10 and 17 instead use conns, labels site and site2, and the default omop handle. For those chapters, replace the two local lines assigning practice and conns at their paired setup with this complete variant:

library(dsOMOPClient)
library(DSOpal)
builder <- DSI::newDSLoginBuilder()
builder$append(server = "site", url = "<server-a-url>",
  user = "<user-a>", password = "<password-a>",
  driver = "OpalDriver", profile = "<profile-a>")
builder$append(server = "site2", url = "<server-b-url>",
  user = "<user-b>", password = "<password-b>",
  driver = "OpalDriver", profile = "<profile-b>")
conns <- DSI::datashield.login(builder$build(), assign = FALSE)
ds.omop.connect(
  resource = list(site = "<project-a>.<questionnaire-resource-a>",
                  site2 = "<project-b>.<questionnaire-resource-b>"),
  conns = conns)

Use resources containing the study’s questionnaire concepts. In chapter 10 this replaces the paired book_switch() block; in chapter 17 it replaces the initial book_connect() block. Keep site and site2 because chapter 17 selects each connection by name. These examples only attach existing resources: local practice-data options do not create data on an Opal server.

Exercise 1: choose the lab resource

Open the numeric resource and request its person count. How can you tell that you are no longer querying GiBleed?

Solution

practice <- book_switch("numeric")
conns <- practice$conns
knitr::kable(as.data.frame(ds.omop.table.stats("person", conns = conns)$per_site$site))
rows persons
25 25

The person count is 25, meaning 25–29 people. That band contains Synthea27Nj’s 28 people and is far below GiBleed’s 2,694. Chapter 1 explains these bands.

Exercise 2: reconnect after finishing

Close the numeric session, then open GiBleed again. Confirm the database with a person count, rather than checking only that a connection has a name.

Solution

book_disconnect()
practice <- book_connect("gibleed")
conns <- practice$conns
knitr::kable(as.data.frame(ds.omop.table.stats("person", conns = conns)$per_site$site))
rows persons
2690 2690

The count is back to the 2,690–2,694 band. Disconnect closes the database handle; logout closes the DataSHIELD session. book_disconnect() performs both steps and clears the practice helper’s session record. Opening a new session starts new work.

Recap

Your working folder contains the helpers, the practice data are loaded, and conns lets you send requests to the selected database.
